lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The armoury door has not moved in a hundred and seventeen years, and it moves now, badly, with two people on the bar.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Rifles in grease paper. Powder in sealed tins. And at the back, on a rack, forty hand-forged blades from the founding year, still oiled, because somebody has been coming down here to oil them.

lines.speaker: dax
lines.text: That's Ash Camp steel. Those are our forge marks — that one's my great-grandmother's, she stamped a notch in the tang, look. Captain sends the signal tonight, they'll be on this wall by morning.

lines.speaker: ade
lines.text: Signal's sent. It went out while you were still deciding, because I know what a person looks like when they have already decided.

lines.speaker: ade
lines.text: Whatever you are, Auditor, you were the right thing to come up those stairs.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: Something is wrong. Listen — not to the valley. The Wardens are not in the valley.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Board was waiting. Not for the armoury; for the decision. Somebody down there knew which way it would go before you did.
